title: Divergent HIF isoform association is linked to hypoxia responses in Mesenchymal stromal cells and human dermal fibroblasts
task: Characterize divergent hypoxia-adaptive programs between MSCs and fibroblasts
key_results: MSCs exhibited 2-4 fold more differentially expressed genes than HDFs under hypoxia; MSC responses centered on HIF1A while HDF responses showed stronger HIF2A/HIF3A association
comments: The finding that phenotypically similar cell types employ fundamentally different HIF isoform-dependent strategies under stress is important for understanding stromal plasticity in regenerative contexts.

model_io.model: Comparative transcriptomics (MSCs vs HDFs)

hypotheses.hypothesis: MSCs and HDFs engage equivalent adaptive programs under hypoxia despite phenotypic overlap
hypotheses.result: Rejected; cell-type-specific regulatory architectures revealed with distinct HIF isoform dependencies

title: The marine drug plitidepsin alleviates osteoporosis in estrogen-deficient mice by suppressing ROS-mediated NRF2/HO-1 signaling and osteoclast formation
task: Evaluate plitidepsin efficacy in suppressing osteoclastogenesis and estrogen-deficiency bone loss
key_results: Plitidepsin suppressed RANKL-induced osteoclast formation and reduced trabecular bone loss in OVX mice; mechanism involves ROS attenuation and NRF2/HO-1 pathway activation
comments: The dual targeting of osteoclast differentiation and oxidative stress through a single marine compound is therapeutically promising, though in vivo bone mass quantification metrics could be more explicit.

model_io.model: Mouse bone marrow-derived macrophage osteoclastogenesis assay
Ovariectomized mouse osteoporosis model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Plitidepsin inhibits osteoclastogenesis through ROS-mediated NRF2/HO-1 signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ROS suppression and enhanced antioxidant defense accompanied reduced osteoclast differentiation

title: Beauvericin exhibits antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer cells: Integrative analysis suggests potential modulation of the KEAP1-NRF2-HMOX1 axis and survival signaling pathways
task: Characterize beauvericin antitumor mechanisms in pancreatic cancer cells
key_results: Beauvericin reduced Mia PaCa-2 cell viability (IC₅₀ = 1.45 µM) and induced 50% apoptosis at 2 µM; molecular docking predicted KEAP1 binding (docking score -9.45 kcal/mol) with downstream attenuation of AKT, ERK1/2, STAT3 phosphorylation
comments: The computational predictions of KEAP1/NRF2 modulation require experimental validation (e.g., NRF2 stabilization assays, KEAP1 mutation studies) to confirm the proposed mechanism versus off-target effects.

model_io.model: Mia PaCa-2 pancreatic cancer cell line
Molecular docking and dynamics simulations
Quantitative proteomics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Beauvericin directly binds KEAP1 and modulates NRF2-dependent survival signaling
hypotheses.result: Supported by computational docking and modulation of KEAP1/NRF2 expression, but mechanistic validation pending

title: 3-O-Acetylrubiarbonol B induces apoptosis of colorectal cancer cells by activating JNK/p38 MAPK and ROS generation
task: Elucidate apoptotic mechanisms of 3-O-Acetylrubiarbonol B in colorectal cancer cells
key_results: ARu-B induced apoptosis in HCT116 and oxaliplatin-resistant HCT116-OxR cells (IC₅₀ 5.4 and 4.0 µM respectively) via JNK/p38 MAPK phosphorylation, ROS generation, and caspase activation
comments: The compound's efficacy against drug-resistant CRC is notable, though the mechanism appears to converge on canonical apoptotic pathways rather than exploiting novel resistance bypass mechanisms.

model_io.model: HCT116 colorectal cancer cell line (parental and oxaliplatin-resistant)

hypotheses.hypothesis: JNK and p38 MAPK phosphorylation are essential for ARu-B-induced apoptosis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; kinase inhibitors prevented cytotoxicity

hypotheses.hypothesis: ROS generation mediates apoptosis downstream of MAPK activation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; NAC pretreatment blocked apoptotic induction
